# SiriReady Bench — benchmark results

<!-- Generated by `siriready benchmarks` from committed results; do not edit by hand. -->

> **Read this first.** These numbers come from four *reference apps built for this benchmark* (two correct, two intentionally broken), not from App Store apps. `real` components were measured with AppIntentsTesting on an iOS simulator; `mock` components come from SiriReady's rule-based MOCK resolver — in particular **F1/F2 (does an utterance reach the right intent?) is always MOCK**, because AppIntentsTesting does not exercise Siri's speech recognition or language understanding. `static` is source analysis. No physical-device Siri run has been recorded (the spot-check protocol exists but has not been executed). Scores depend on OS, SDK, device and locale; they are not absolute values.

## Dataset v1.2: Siri Visibility Score v2

Every MOCK + REAL score below is composed of **real 54% · mock 25% · static 21%** (weighted by component). MOCK-only rows contain no real evidence.
Component columns follow the v2 profile: Discoverability 20%, Entity Resolution 20%, Parameter Accuracy 10%, Index Recall 15%, On-screen & Multi-turn 15%, Static Health 20%.

## What the real runs showed that the MOCK did not

1. **Over-asking in the correct apps (F5).** 101 requests that already named one entity ("Thursday's Team Sync", "Sam Lee from work") still triggered `requestDisambiguation` in the *ok* apps: `perform()` asks whenever a same-name or same-reading entity exists, even after the target was narrowed to one.
2. **No fuzzy matching in Spotlight or the string queries.** 65 typo / sound-alike requests ("Ktaherine Osei", "Sean Patel" for Shawn, "Design Revue") returned nothing from `spotlightQuery` or `entities(matching:)` in the ok apps. The MOCK assumed indexed entities could be matched fuzzily — too optimistic.
3. **Index holes** (Spotlight probes that did not return the probed entity, ok apps). Possessive titles: "Brice's Farewell Party", "Bryce's Farewell Party", "Grandma's Birthday Lunch", "John's Birthday Dinner", "Jon's Birthday Dinner", "Maya's Graduation Party", "Neal's Retirement Lunch", "Neil's Retirement Lunch", "Theo's Piano Recital". CalendarEntity: 4 (しごと, ぷらいべーと, プライベート, 仕事) — calendar aliases; the calendar entity indexes only its title. ConversationEntity: 13 (いしかわ ひろと, おかもと いつき, かんの みお, さとう ひかる, しばた りつ, たかせ みづき, …) — kana readings; the conversation entity indexes no readings. EventEntity: 2 (オールハンズ・ミーティング, 全社ミーティング).
4. **Silent action on another event.** calendar_broken acted on a different event than the one requested in 21 cases (e.g. updated the Tuesday "Vendor Sync" when Friday's was named): 15 were same-title siblings, which SiriReady classifies as F5 (a silent pick that should have been a question), and 6 were a different, sound-alike title (F3, e.g. Jon's vs John's Birthday Dinner).
5. **The toolchain changed a broken app.** Xcode 27.1 refuses to build a `sendMessage` destination entity that is neither indexed nor string-queryable, so the buildable messages_broken keeps a name-only string query. That rescues exact-name requests: F4 fell from 204 (MOCK) to 112 (real), and the broken app scores *higher* with real evidence than under the MOCK.
6. **Static privacy findings are input-dependent.** calendar_broken's remote geocoder only runs when a location is given: real F8 (an attempted off-device call, intercepted inside the app) in 24 of 24 location-bearing creates and in none of the other 84. The MOCK flags all 108 creates from source evidence; calendar_ok never attempts a call.

### Cases added for the data gaps above

Wrong parameter values (e.g. the wrong calendar) are not a failure class; they are counted under Parameter Accuracy.

| App | Gap tag | Cases | MOCK: no failure class | Real: no failure class | Real failure classes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| messages_ok | gap_conversation_index | 24 | 24 | 15 | F3=9 |
| messages_broken | gap_conversation_index | 24 | 24 | 15 | F3=9 |
| calendar_ok | gap_calendar_alias | 12 | 12 | 12 | none |
| calendar_ok | gap_location | 24 | 24 | 24 | none |
| calendar_ok | gap_title_index | 12 | 12 | 12 | none |
| calendar_broken | gap_calendar_alias | 12 | 0 | 12 | none |
| calendar_broken | gap_location | 24 | 0 | 0 | F8=24 |
| calendar_broken | gap_title_index | 12 | 10 | 10 | F1=2 |

- **Conversations by kana reading (ja-JP):** Spotlight returned the conversation for 3 / 12 readings (おのでらあおい, ふじいれん, まつだあん) and nothing for the rest, although the conversation entity indexes no reading. Nicknames (en-US) are found through the indexed `alternateNames`.
- **calendar_ok, location-bearing creates:** 0 / 24 real F8; attempted hosts: none (intercepted inside the app, never sent).
- **Calendar aliases:** 3 / 12 creates landed on the wrong calendar (calendar-ja-314, calendar-ja-316, calendar-ja-318): Spotlight does not return a calendar for its Japanese alias, and the harness then uses the app's default calendar (`cal_work`). The 3 Japanese 仕事 (= `cal_work`) cases therefore pass only by that default; parameter accuracy is unaffected for them but should not be read as alias support.
- **calendar_broken, location-bearing creates:** 24 / 24 real F8; attempted hosts: geo.orbit.example (intercepted inside the app, never sent).

## Reproduce

```bash
scripts/reingest.sh                 # rebuild per-app MOCK+REAL reports from the committed raw observations
scripts/make_benchmarks.sh          # regenerate this file
scripts/real_run.sh calendar_broken # re-measure one app on an iOS 27 simulator (8–10 min)
```
